assignments.reason: בְּחִינַת לֵאָה is the spiritual dimension of Leah. The Torah defines Leah as 'שֶׁהִיא בָּעֹרֶף, שֶׁהִיא נֻקְבָּא רִאשׁוֹנָה' — she is in the nape, the first feminine. By essential nature this is Leah herself as a kabbalistic principle, identical to the לאה node already in Package 1. She belongs to the ערף/Luz hidden-place cluster as the concealed feminine dimension of the nape zone.

בְּחִינַת רָחֵל is the spiritual dimension of Rachel — the revealed feminine, the ultimate holy destination. The Torah states that Jacob's entire intention was for Rachel, and that through the bechina of Leah (the first/hidden) one can arrive at the bechina of Rachel. Rachel represents the fulfilled, revealed goal — the same domain of holy attainment as the Temple (בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ), resurrection (תְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים), and consolation (עִקַּר נֶחָמוֹתֵינוּ) in Package 2. By essential nature she is the holy destination, not the hidden pathway.

נִכְנָסִין לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ (entering the Temple) is the act of arriving at the holy destination. The בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ itself is already in Package 2 as the sacred goal reached through the Luz pathway. By essential nature, 'entering the Temple' belongs to the same domain of holy arrival and consolation — it is the actualization of the Temple's promise. The Torah states: 'וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִכְנָסִין לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ' — after the Leah/nape stage, one enters the Temple, which is the domain of Package 2.
